headline: Corn and beans ease back as harvest pressure builds
lead: Corn is at $4.75½ overnight, down 2¾ cents from Thursday's $4.78¼ settle, and beans are off 6 cents at $12.58¼. Fund selling has picked up as combines roll and bushels keep piling into the bins. Basis stays at seasonal lows with harvest in full swing.
teaser: Corn and beans slip again as fund selling meets a big harvest.

one_number.unit: straight monthly cuts to 2026 beef output
one_number.context: USDA's October WASDE marked the eighth straight downgrade to beef production, a sign the cow herd has stopped shrinking but hasn't started growing.

sections.title: Grain slips on fund selling
sections.body:
- Corn is at **$4.75½** overnight, down from Thursday's $4.78¼, with wheat off 9¼ cents at $6.60.
- AgWeb reports more fund selling hit corn and beans as harvest pressure builds across the Belt.
- Some traders are questioning whether USDA's 181.2 bushel corn yield estimate is too high, which would cut the other way.
sections.so_what: Funds are selling into the harvest, not waiting for the yield debate to settle.

sections.title: Cattle and feeders firm overnight
sections.body:
- Live cattle are at **$225.95** overnight, up 0.9% from Thursday's $223.90, and feeders gained 0.7% to $343.38.
- Beef magazine notes October's WASDE marked the eighth straight monthly cut to 2026 beef production.
- Hogs sit flat at $75.55 and milk firmed slightly to $15.26.
sections.so_what: A herd that's stopped shrinking still isn't growing, and cattle keep finding support.

sections.title: Crude heads for a weekly gain
sections.body: - WTI is at **$95.73** overnight, down 2.3% from Thursday's $97.97, but still on track for a weekly gain.
sections.so_what: Diesel stays the tighter, pricier story even as crude itself eases back today.

outside_the_pit.title: Bill would widen cattle insurance to rebuild the herd
outside_the_pit.body: A House bill, the More Beef, Lower Prices Act, would add bred cattle, replacement heifers and cull cows to USDA's livestock risk protection program starting crop year 2027.

watch_list.desc: Corn back under $4.75 would say harvest supply is beating the fund short-covering bounce.
Crude holding above $95 through the weekend would confirm the Hormuz premium is sticking, not fading.
Crop Progress report; a faster-than-expected harvest pace could add more pressure on corn and beans.

source_summary: CME/CBOT overnight quotes, USDA WASDE, AgWeb, feedstuffs.com, beefmagazine.com, oilprice.com

lines: Corn harvest price so far: $4.92 vs $4.62 projected (+6.5%), 11 of 22 trading days in.
Soybeans harvest price so far: $12.85 vs $11.09 projected (+15.9%), 11 of 22 trading days in.
harvest_clock.note: Average of the daily CBOT settles through Oct 15, figured the way USDA RMA does. RMA posts corn at $4.93. RMA posts soybeans at $12.87. Window and projected price: USDA RMA, as of Oct 15. Oct 1-31 window, most states.
